notes: The San Francisco City Planning Commission's minutes of its regular and special meetings, January to December 1974, from the volumes the San Francisco Public Library contributed to the Internet Archive (28minutesofsanfran1974sa, 29minutesofsanfran1974sa). Pages were split from the hOCR search text on the Internet Archive page index, counting the viewer page among the leaves scandata.xml does not mark addToAccessFormats=false (checked against the scan of 24minutesofsanfran1973sa n10, page 4 of the 4 January 1973 minutes). Every page is dated from the meeting header it sits under. Four kinds of finding: what the Commission decided about a property, dated to the meeting that decided it; what the minutes state stood on or occupied the property; dated past facts the minutes state about a building; and landmark designations. A proposal on its own is not a finding. A Board of Supervisors action the minutes report without its own date is framed 'by' the date of the meeting that reported it. The minutes name applicants, owners, attorneys, objectors, commissioners and staff throughout; the reader spec (in research/sources/sf-planning-commission-minutes.md, under Reader spec) barred all of them from every field, and kept companies, institutions, named buildings and architects.

coverage.remaining: Every page of the two 1974 volumes (28minutesofsanfran1974sa, January-June; 29minutesofsanfran1974sa, July-December) was read. Volumes 30-39 (1975-1980) and 40-58 (1994-2005) remain. Of the 209 unresolved, 143 print no street number: Parkmerced, the St. Mary's Hospital and St. Francis Hospital master plans, the Nob Hill rezoning's named towers on corners, the Marshall Square symphony-hall site, the Western Addition mini-park transfers, Muni substation and Metro Center sites, the Hunters Point shipyard, Lincoln Park and Fort Miley; 26 have no EAS record at the number; 5 are condominiums waiting on #446 (1200 California, 1520 O'Farrell, 1170 Sacramento); the rest are ranges split across parcels or lots of several parcels.
coverage.note: 801 OCR pages with text out of 1,498 scanned leaves, read by six parallel readers from one written spec (the dossier's Reader spec section); 48 meetings dated from their own headers; 424 findings: 182 statements of what stood on a property, 158 decisions, 59 dated past facts, 25 landmark designations. Every quote was re-anchored mechanically against its own page (424 of 424). 215 resolved: 178 by the EAS join on a printed number, 37 by hand — 6 by the record's own block and lot, 31 by name on a building the site already carries (the Goodman Building and the City of Paris Building, whose printed numbers 1117 and 199 Geary have no EAS record; the Pacific Union Club, the War Memorial, the Orpheum, the Gaylord, Laguna Honda Hospital). Four EAS joins onto lots with no roll row were taken back to unresolved as condominiums. 191 published on 91 pages (51 of them seeded); 24 declined: 14 already on the page from the Article 10 reports, the National Register or another source, 3 later reports of a refusal published from the vote itself, 1 repeat of a 1973 finding, 4 procedural, 1 OCR-misread year, 1 address that was a company's office. Two conflicts recorded: 2107 Broadway dated 1896 against the roll's 1905 (stated in unknowns and building.completed_conflict) and the Stanyan House's flanking houses, 1892 against 1885 (already stated on the page). The year's distinctive sitting is 27 June 1974: fifteen residential care facilities licensed by the state, each dated, sized and given its start year.
